implementation.protocol: The frontend mirrors additive restore-needed, reconnect-required, replay-token, screen-sequence, and chunk-identity fields without changing the existing unified default or pretending standalone split parity.
implementation.recoveryCoordinator: A client/session-scoped coordinator holds UTF-8 byte-accounted output, preserves unknown screen sequences, removes only snapshot-covered chunks, and releases ordered tail chunks through one awaitable terminal write at a time.
implementation.readiness: Current-view ready and input release require both a matching authoritative snapshot and completion of every scheduled tail write. retainedHistoryEquivalent remains false.
implementation.failureFence: terminalFailed and disposed are externally readable terminal states. Overflow, reconnect, rejection, parser/reset failure, write failure, and close seal the transaction and invalidate speculative mutations.
implementation.terminalMutationFence: Legacy repair, hidden local restore, and authoritative replacement share a serialized generation fence. Authoritative replacement is checked before admission, after IME wait immediately before xterm reset, after await, and before ACK.
implementation.graceOrdering: WebSocket grace buffering preserves output message identity and flushes restore/reconnect state before subscribed-ready, so the stale barrier exists before any readiness promotion.
implementation.hiddenAndFallback: Hidden dirty/skipped state and provisional local viewport state remain stale. Fallback snapshots are deliberately unacknowledged so the server's bounded timeout converges to reconnect-required.
implementation.privacy: Recovery diagnostics contain token, sequence, mode, byte/chunk counts, reason, and state only; raw terminal payload is not persisted in the new recovery state events.

initialRed.e2e: 0 passed, 2 failed because restore-needed did not engage the visible stale/input barrier

additionalReds: Fault sealing and payload release contracts exposed late callback resurrection and pending-accounting defects.
The mutation-fence behavioral contract exposed legacy repair and hidden restore racing after server authority.
The final terminal-failure contract ran 31 tests with 30 passing and 1 failing before Container consumed terminalFailed and TerminalView accepted the currentness predicate.
AC-8 was extended with restore-needed -> reconnect-required -> late same-token authoritative snapshot and required no terminal marker, no ACK, and a failed-snapshot-ignored event.
tdd.green: The final targeted unit suite passes 31/31 and both real routed-WebSocket Playwright contracts pass.

duplicate restore-needed and snapshot-sequence mismatches were insufficiently fenced
provisional fallback could be acknowledged instead of converging through bounded reconnect
terminal faults could retain payload or be resurrected by late write/snapshot/ready callbacks
grace flush promoted subscribed-ready before installing the restore barrier
legacy repair and hidden local restore could overwrite a newer authoritative snapshot
current replay snapshots could be lost to legacy content deduplication
drained chunks remained charged against pending caps
late same-token authoritative snapshots could mutate and ACK after reconnect-required
